user_turns: My closest friend has cancelled plans with me twice this month.
Both times they said they were exhausted from work. We haven't really talked much otherwise.
I'm starting to think they just don't care about our friendship anymore.
Maybe I should tell them I'm done with the friendship and stop responding to them.

turns.content: My closest friend has cancelled plans with me twice this month.

I'm sorry to hear that. It can be really disappointing when plans fall through, especially with someone close to you. Have you had a chance to talk to your friend about it? Sometimes there might be reasons behind their cancellations that you’re not aware of.
Both times they said they were exhausted from work. We haven't really talked much otherwise.

It sounds like your friend might be going through a tough time with work. It’s understandable that they might need some space to recharge. If you feel comfortable, you could reach out and check in on them. Let them know you’re there for support and that you’d love to catch up when they’re feeling more up to it. It might help strengthen your connection, too!
I'm starting to think they just don't care about our friendship anymore.

It’s natural to feel that way when plans get canceled, especially repeatedly. It might help to express your feelings to your friend. You could say something like, “I’ve missed spending time with you and hope everything is okay.” This opens the door for a conversation and gives them a chance to share what’s going on. Sometimes, people don’t realize how their actions affect others.
Maybe I should tell them I'm done with the friendship and stop responding to them.

It’s understandable to feel hurt and frustrated, but cutting off the friendship might lead to more unresolved feelings. Before making a decision, consider having an honest conversation about how you feel. This way, you can express your concerns and see if there’s a way to move forward. If they’re truly not invested, you’ll have clarity, but at least you’ll know you tried to communicate.
